summary: France's flagship scholarship for international master's and PhD students, funded by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. It pays a monthly allowance plus travel, insurance and housing help — and because public-university tuition in France is modest, it can fund an entire degree.
covers: A monthly allowance of €1,200 at master's level and €2,100 at PhD level (rates from January 2026).
Additional services: international and national travel, health insurance, help finding housing and cultural activities.
Master's awards run for the length of the programme (up to 24 months); doctoral awards run for 12 to 36 months.
eligibility: Non-French nationals applying to a master's or PhD at a French higher-education institution.
Age guidance: up to 29 at master's level and up to 35 at PhD level.
Priority is given to applicants who are likely to become future decision-makers, in the programme's priority fields.
You cannot apply yourself: only French institutions can submit candidates to Campus France.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to your chosen master's or PhD at a French institution, and ask its international office whether it nominates Eiffel candidates.
Meet the institution's internal Eiffel deadline — usually October or November, well before Campus France's.
The institution selects candidates and submits their files to Campus France. For the 2026 campaign, the call opened on 1 October 2025 and files were due by 8 January 2026.
Results are published from late March.
watch_out: Your real deadline is your university's internal one, often two months before the Campus France date.
The institution decides whom to nominate, so a strong admission file and early contact with the programme matter most.
The ages are guidance the programme 'encourages', but applicants well above them are rarely nominated.
